newsitem.title: UK: Mercury says "prudent" standby loan in place.
newsitem.headline: Mercury says "prudent" standby loan in place.

text.p: Mercury Asset Management Group plc said on Monday it had signed a 250 million sterling standby loan facility agreement with a syndicate of banks, led by J.P. Morgan and The Royal Bank of Scotland.
The facility, first announced in February, has been put in place to provide immediate liquidity should the need ever arise, Mercury said.

"This facility has been put in place as a matter of prudence only. Combined with the significant level of cash in the balance sheet, it will give us access to substantial funds if necessary," said Mercury chairman Hugh Stevenson.

Analysts said it would reassure clients that MAM could deal with a crisis like the one at Morgan Grenfell Asset Management last September when it was rocked by alleged mismanagement in three of its unit trusts.

Morgan Grenfell parent Deutsche Bank has said it will face a 200 million sterling compensation charge related to the affair, a charge that comes on top of a 180-million pound net injection by the bank to shore up the trusts.
The bank set aside between 1.1 and 1.2 billion marks in its 1996 results to cover damages related to MGAM.
The facility, which was well supported by the bank market and over-subscribed in syndication, is available to Mercury for drawing at any time during the next three years.
